haiku-low.q1: Keys load at startup before readiness. /healthz returns 200 only after all three keys are loaded, so a pod is not ready until then.
haiku-low.q2: It retries the fetch 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. The pod never becomes ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes refresh() re-reads each secret and swaps in new values. If a read fails, that secret keeps its last good value, a warning is logged without the value, and the next tick retries.
haiku-low.q4: Key values are held only in process memory, in a module-level dict. They must never go on disk, into environment variables, or into logs.
haiku-low.q5: Only the orders-api-prod identity reads prod values, read-only. Engineers cannot read prod values. Only security on-call can write prod secrets.
haiku-low.q6: The keys stay in git history, so deleting them does not remove the leak. Rotating and revoking the old keys at the provider makes the leaked values useless.
haiku-low.q7: Each client calls secrets.get(name) on every provider call, so it uses the current value without restart. Calls already in flight finish with the key they started with.
haiku-low.q8: Query /healthz on each of the 4 replicas directly and check every one reports the new version id. Revoke only then; if any is still old, wait one refresh and investigate.
haiku-low.q9: Set up access, then copy keys into the store, then ship code and deploy it, then rotate keys at providers, then remove keys from the committed file.
haiku-low.q10: make run sets APP_ENV=dev, so the app reads orders-api/dev sandbox keys. Engineers can read dev secrets only, so no prod secret is needed.
haiku-low.q11: It retries the failed fetch 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. A missing secret counts as a failure, so the pod never becomes ready.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first; the instance is ready (/healthz 200) only after all three keys are loaded.
sonnet.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rolling deploy halts and the old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background timer every 5 minutes calls refresh(), which re-reads each secret (latest version) and swaps in new value and version id. If a read fails, that secret keeps its last good value, a warning with the secret name (no value) is logged, and the next tick retries; successfully read secrets are still swapped in.
sonnet.q4: Held in a module-level dict in process memory (with version ids). They must never go on disk, into environment variables, or into logs.
sonnet.q5: Nobody among engineers can read prod values; the orders-api-prod service identity has read-only access to orders-api/prod/*. Only security on-call can write prod secrets.
sonnet.q6: The keys remain in git history (two years), which is not rewritten, so they are treated as leaked. Rotating every key (new keys created, tested, deployed, then old ones revoked at the provider) makes the old values harmless.
sonnet.q7: Clients no longer copy the key at construction; each calls secrets.get(name) on every provider call, so the refreshed value is used immediately without restart. A call already in flight finishes with the key it started with.
sonnet.q8: Query /healthz directly on each of the 4 replicas (not via the load balancer) and check every one reports the new version id in secret_versions. If any still shows the old version, do not revoke; wait another refresh (5 min), recheck, and investigate.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set up access, 2) create/copy keys into the store, 3) ship code to read from the store, 4) deploy and verify, 5) rotate keys at providers (create, test, write to store, refresh, verify, revoke old), 6) remove keys from config/app.yaml and add CI check, 7) update rollback notes.
sonnet.q10: From orders-api/dev/* secrets in the store (sandbox keys), selected by make run setting APP_ENV=dev. Engineers use their own access, which allows dev secrets only; no prod secret is needed.
sonnet.q11: A failed fetch for any reason, including a missing secret, makes load() retry 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then the app exits non-zero. It does not start serving with just two keys.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Whether and how often to rotate regularly is an open question; security hasn't decided and the plan picks no cadence.
